# A density-only obstruction to paying an asymmetric original mass

This is an exact obstruction to one auxiliary-measure inference. It is not a counterexample to OC and does not realize a midpoint measure of two prescribed actual endpoint bodies. The missing information is precisely the common Minkowski support and the unused endpoint cap mass.

## 1. Explicit body, submeasure, and numerical data

Let K be a regular six-dimensional simplex of volume one, with vertices P_1,...,P_7, centroid g, and barycentric coordinates lambda_1,...,lambda_7. Put

    T_i=P_i+(3/8)(K-P_i),
    U=union_(i=1)^7 T_i,
    w=|U|=7(3/8)^6,
    a=(1/100)^6, b=1, k=1,
    v_*=((a^(1/6)+b^(1/6))/2)^6=(101/200)^6.

Each T_i is exactly the portion of K with lambda_i>=5/8. The copies have disjoint interiors, since two such barycentric coordinates cannot sum to at most one. Define the absolutely continuous measure

    eta=(a/w)1_U dx.

It has mass a, support in K, and centroid g by permutation symmetry. Its density satisfies the same volume ceiling that an unequal-endpoint midpoint coupling would supply:

    eta <= (a/v_*)1_K dx <=1_K dx,

because the exact positive difference is

    w-v_*=92164729387/32000000000000>0.

Every measure 1_K dx+c eta, c>=0, has centroid g. The example therefore also treats every scalar choice of coefficient in such a centroid rule.

## 2. Seven exact ambient continuous caps

For each i put H_i={lambda_i>=1/7}. These seven closed halfspaces cover K: the seven barycentric coordinates sum to one. Their K-volume is

    Gamma_6=(6/7)^6=46656/117649.

The whole own corner T_i is in H_i. For j!=i, barycentric coordinates on T_j give lambda_i=(3/8)u_i, where u is the barycentric coordinate on the original simplex. Thus H_i cuts from T_j the fraction

    (1-8/21)^6=(13/21)^6.

Consequently, for nu=1_K dx+eta, all seven caps have exactly the same mass

    nu(H_i)=Gamma_6+a c_6,
    c_6=[1+6(13/21)^6]/7=38242325/200120949.

The exact comparison is

    Gamma_6/2-c_6=1438603/200120949>0.

Every point of K belongs to at least one H_i. It follows directly, without an assumption about an attaining minimizing halfspace, that

    sup_(y in K) inf_(closed H containing y) nu(H)
       <=Gamma_6+a c_6
       <(Gamma_6/2)(k+a+b).

Points outside K have zero depth for nu, by strict separation from the compact convex support K, so allowing all continuous points does not repair this auxiliary upper bound. In particular none of the centroids of K+c eta can do so. Closed cap boundaries have zero nu mass.

## 3. Exact scope of the obstruction

The constructed eta satisfies the mass, density ceiling, support-in-K and centroid properties retained by the bounded-density dual. Those data alone do not imply that the auxiliary cap budget |K intersect H|+eta(H) pays the original asymmetric three-fiber mass k+a+b. The obstruction persists even if that auxiliary measure's best center is used instead of its particular centroid.

There is no claim that this eta is the midpoint law of full convex bodies A and B having volumes a and b, or that the original endpoint cap sum equals eta(H). Indeed conv(support eta)=K, whereas an actual midpoint law must also live in the one common body (A+B)/2. This extra shape condition is absent from the relaxation above. The larger endpoint also leaves a nonnegative cap remainder after the marginal factor a/b is used. Either fact can defeat the auxiliary obstruction in an actual body. Thus this certificate closes only the density-only attempted promotion, not the actual unequal-endpoint or general OC problem.
